title: PRA operations in the Python SDK and Ansible approvals

prose.text: SDK and Ansible calls for PRA objects map onto a few operations. Terraform behavior for PRA is in the provider-defect subjects, and the segment reconciliation in Ansible is in [[zpa.app-segments.ansible-children]].

Terraform delete and credential-rule defects are in [[zpa.terraform.delete-paths]] and [[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes]]; approval validation and PRA console read defects are in [[zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity]]; secret handling is in [[shared.terraform.credential-handling]].
Two approvals with the same emails and applications are indistinguishable to the module: {{ansible-approval-lookup-ignores-windows}}
Whether the module can pick between approvals that differ only by window is open {{gap:approval-identity-windows}}.
Whether the credential-pool endpoints the SDKs call are a supported API surface is open [[zpa.api.pra-wire:credential-pool-not-in-contract]].

checks.do: Whether a pool-exhaustion investigation can read which credentials the pool holds through the pool-info operation.
Whether an approval payload omits working_hours, which current SDK and Ansible versions allow.
Whether two Ansible approvals for the same emails but different applications are intended.

pool-credential-info.statement: The Python SDK's get_credential_pool_info(pool_id) calls GET /credential-pool/{pool_id}/credential and returns the credential information mapped to the pool.

quotes: def get_credential_pool_info(self, pool_id: str
Given Privileged credential pool id gets mapped privileged credential info
/credential-pool/{pool_id}/credential
http_method = "get".upper()

expired-approval-cleanup.statement: The Python SDK's expired_approval(microtenant_id) deletes all expired privileged approvals through DELETE /approval/expired.

quotes: def expired_approval(self, microtenant_id: str = None)
Deletes all expired privileged approvals.
/approval/expired
http_method = "delete".upper()

bulk-console-add.statement: The Python SDK's add_bulk_console(consoles) creates several PRA consoles in one call through POST /praConsole/bulk.

quotes: def add_bulk_console(self, consoles: list, **kwargs)
Adds multiple Privileged Remote Access (PRA) consoles in bulk.
/praConsole/bulk
http_method = "post".upper()

working-hours-optional.statement: In the Python SDK pra_approval, working_hours is optional: time conversion defaults to UTC when it is omitted, and workingHours is sent only when the caller supplies it, because the API rejects a partial or empty workingHours object. The 1.9.34 release note records a working_hours fix.

quotes: # Only include working hours when explicitly provided. The API rejects a
# partial/empty workingHours object because its sub-fields (start time, etc.)
time_zone = working_hours.get("time_zone") or "UTC"
Fixed ZPA `pra_approval` attribute `working_hours`.

working-hours-optional.conditions: Statement changed: "Since 1.9.34" removed; the release note says only that the pra_approval working_hours attribute was fixed, and the omission behavior is from the code.

ansible-working-hours.statement: The ZPA Ansible collection made working_hours optional for zpa_pra_approval in 2.2.5 and fixed update to send the intended payload instead of the raw existing approval.

quotes: made `working_hours` truly optional so approvals can be created and updated without it.
Fixed `zpa_pra_approval` update to send the intended payload instead of the raw existing approval
description: "Privileged Approval WorkHours configuration."

ansible-approval-match.statement: The Ansible zpa_pra_approval module selects an existing approval by email_ids and, when supplied, application_ids. An approval with the same email set and a different application set is skipped, so the requested approval is created rather than overwriting the unrelated one.

quotes: # applications the approval grants access to. The same email can hold
# several approvals, one per application segment, so matching on
# email_ids alone would select an unrelated approval and update it in
# place instead of creating the approval that was asked for.
for approval_ in result: if sorted(approval_.email_ids or []) != sorted(email_ids or []): continue
if desired_application_ids is not None: current_application_ids = sorted( app.get("id") for app in (approval_.applications or []) if app.get("id") )
if current_application_ids != sorted(desired_application_ids): continue existing_approval = approval_.as_dict() break

ansible-approval-lookup-ignores-windows.statement: The Ansible approval lookup compares the sorted email set and, when application IDs are supplied, the sorted application ID set, and does not compare the approval's start or end window.

quotes: for approval_ in result: if sorted(approval_.email_ids or []) != sorted(email_ids or []): continue
if desired_application_ids is not None: current_application_ids = sorted( app.get("id") for app in (approval_.applications or []) if app.get("id") )
if current_application_ids != sorted(desired_application_ids): continue existing_approval = approval_.as_dict() break

ansible-approval-lookup-ignores-windows.conditions: No line of the lookup reads startTime or endTime; the absence is read from the loop quoted.

approval-identity-windows.title: Whether approvals may share an email set and application set while having different time windows
approval-identity-windows.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-82. Unverified legacy statement: Ansible 2.2.11 and later distinguishes approval candidates by email set plus the requested application set, but its lookup does not compare start and end windows, and it is not known whether two approvals may legitimately share those sets with different windows or how automation should select between them. Create two approvals with the same emails and applications and different windows in a scratch tenant, then run the module against each.
approval-identity-windows.blocks: selecting the right existing approval when only the window differs
